bug_semantics: AES-CBC decrypt (default mode) PKCS#7-style unpads by reading the last plaintext byte as pad length and taking a data-dependent path when that length is invalid (0 or greater than the block size). In the pre-fix form the length predicate used boolean `||`, which short-circuits so a zero pad byte skips `$length > $this->block_size`; valid vs invalid padding therefore differ in both control flow and wall-clock time, and invalid padding later returns false / throws instead of the stripped plaintext. A chosen-ciphertext attacker who can observe decrypt timing (or the validity signal) can recover CBC plaintext (CWE-208 padding-oracle timing).
flaw_origin: The AES/Rijndael unpad validity branch was first written in c30f3b7e9a73c6579e0b6fa1f99d9cbcaea5ae28 (2009-02-01, Jim Wigginton, SourceForge SVN r20) as Crypt_Rijndael::_unpad: `if ($length > $this->block_size) { user_error(...); return $text; }` else `substr`. Parent a78d7df6 has no Rijndael.php/AES.php (only DES/TripleDES unpad without a length-validity branch). AES 0.1.1 extends Rijndael and calls this unpad after CBC decrypt. a4e72f78 (2009-11-23) mutated the same predicate to `if (!$length || $length > $this->block_size)` (the exact short-circuit later patched); 9bd3c793 switched the invalid path to `return false`; 55ff00cc moved it into Crypt_Base::_unpad; 3.x copied it into SymmetricKey::unpad (throw on invalid). None of those are first-writes. 2026 fix ccc21aef only replaced `||` with non-short-circuit `|`.

reasoning: GHSA-94g3-g5v7-q4jg / CVE-2026-32935 is a live published advisory (CVE.org PUBLISHED, GHSA not withdrawn) for a real CWE-208: phpseclib AES-CBC unpadding leaks padding validity through timing. Decrypt (default CBC) PKCS-unpads using the last plaintext byte as length; invalid length historically took a slower/different path than valid length. The 2026 patch ccc21aef71eb170e9bf819b167e67d1fd9e6e788 is the direct one-line fix on 1.0 (merged to 2.0 then 3.0 SymmetricKey.php), changing short-circuit `||` to bitwise `|` so both length checks always run; it is present in patched tags 1.0.27/2.0.52/3.0.50 and absent from the last unpatched tags. The smallest first-write of that mechanism is c30f3b7e9a73c6579e0b6fa1f99d9cbcaea5ae28, which added Crypt_Rijndael::_unpad with a ciphertext-dependent `if ($length > $this->block_size)` oracle (user_error vs substr) used by AES from 0.1.1. Immediate parent a78d7df66031ee1be64cfab2f8a4ea29f6be182a has no Rijndael/AES file and no equivalent length-validity branch, so introducer_parent_absent is true after parent-tree check. Later a4e72f78 (add `!$length ||`), 9bd3c793 (return false), 55ff00cc (Crypt_Base move), and the 3.x SymmetricKey rename are mutations/moves of the same check, not BICs; using a4e72f78 would also fail the 'BIC precedes affected range' gate because 0.1.1 already shipped the original unpad oracle. The BIC is a 2009 human SVN import (Jim Wigginton / terrafrost@php.net) with no commit-object AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
